findings.message: This round changes the edge filter from `not c.condeferrable` to `not c.condeferred`. The only behaviour that changes is for a key declared `deferrable initially immediate`: it is now an ordering edge, where before it was dropped. No test covers that case. The table in `packages/core/tests/backup-restore-order-154.test.ts:38-41` has only two rows: `deferrable initially deferred` and not deferrable. Both pass with the old filter and with the new one, so nothing fails if the fix is reverted. Fix: add a third row to that table, a two-table cycle of `deferrable initially immediate` keys. Expect it to be refused as a cycle checked at once, the same as non-deferrable keys. Also add a parent/child pair joined by an initially-immediate deferrable key and assert the parent comes before the child.
findings.scenario: Revert line 44 to `not c.condeferrable`, then run backup-restore-order-154.test.ts: every case still passes. Yet a schema with `child.parent_id references parent deferrable` (initially immediate) is ordered without that edge, so the child can load first, and its insert fails at statement end in the drill.

findings.message: The guard only lists files ending in `.spec.ts`. Playwright's default testMatch also picks up `*.test.ts`, `*.spec.tsx`, `*.spec.js` and similar files in `tests/e2e`. A signed-in spec written with one of those extensions runs in the public run and is never checked by this guard. Fix: list files with the same pattern Playwright uses (`/\.(spec|test)\.[cm]?[jt]sx?$/`), so every file either run picks up must be placed on one side.
findings.scenario: Add `tests/e2e/release-chart.test.ts`, which calls `signIn(`. The guard's list skips it, the public run's testIgnore doesn't match it, so it runs with no database, and CI fails as it did on PR #134.
